20641-through-three-campaigns-a-story-of.title: Through Three Campaigns A Story Of Chitral Tirah And Ashanti
20641-through-three-campaigns-a-story-of.creator: G. A. Henty.
20641-through-three-campaigns-a-story-of.description: A book by G. A. Henty.. an illustration of this, three campaigns; namely, the relief of Chitral, the Tirah campaign, and the relief of Coomassie. The first two were conducted in a mountainous country, affording every advantage to the enemy; where passes had to be scaled, torrents to be forded, and deep snow to be crossed.

arxiv-2012-05734.title: Finite Size Effects on the Chiral Phase Transition of Quantum Chromodynamics
arxiv-2012-05734.creator: Shen-Song Wan, Daize Li, Bonan Zhang, Marco Ruggieri
arxiv-2012-05734.description: Abstract We study the effect of periodic boundary conditions on chiral symmetry breaking and its restoration in Quantum Chromodynamics. As an effective model of the effective potential for the quark condensate, we use the quark-meson model, while the theory is quantized in a cubic box of size L L .

arxiv-2104-03637.title: Extending Hierarchical Delta Debugging with Hoisting
arxiv-2104-03637.creator: Dániel Vince, Renáta Hodován, Daniella Bársony and Ákos Kiss
arxiv-2104-03637.description: Abstract Minimizing failing test cases is an important pre-processing step on the path of debugging. If much of a test case that triggered a bug does not contribute to the actual failure, then the time required to fix the bug can increase considerably. However, test case reduction itself can be a time consuming task, especially if done manually.

arxiv-2112-08084.title: Temporally Modulated One-Dimensional Leaky-Wave Holograms
arxiv-2112-08084.creator: Amrollah Amini, Homayoon Oraizi
arxiv-2112-08084.description: Abstract Spatio-temporally modulated impedance surfaces can be good candidates for generation of radiating waves with arbitrary eigenstates by breaking momentum and energy conservations. Here, we present a theoretical framework based on the holographic technique and generalized Floquet-wave expansion to analyze spatio-temporally modulated impedance surfaces. The holographic technique estimates the required impedance distribution to achieve the desired momentum.

arxiv-2203-00108.title: MRI-GAN: A Generalized Approach to Detect DeepFakes using Perceptual Image Assessment
arxiv-2203-00108.creator: Pratikkumar Prajapati pratik.prajapati@gmail.com, Dr. Chris Pollett chris@pollett.org
arxiv-2203-00108.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Pratikkumar Prajapati pratik.prajapati@gmail.com, Dr. Chris Pollett chris@pollett.org. DeepFakes are synthetic videos generated by swapping a face of an original image with the face of somebody else. In this paper, we describe our work to develop general, deep learning-based models to classify DeepFake content. We propose a novel framework for using Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based models, we call MRI-GAN, that utilizes perceptual differences in images to detect synthesized videos. We test our MRI-GAN approach and a plain-frames-based model using the DeepFake Detection Challenge Dataset.

arxiv-2205-01703.title: Improving In-Context Few-Shot Learning via Self-Supervised Training
arxiv-2205-01703.creator: Mingda Chen, Jingfei Du, Ramakanth Pasunuru, Todor Mihaylov, Srini Iyer, Veselin Stoyanov, Zornitsa Kozareva
arxiv-2205-01703.description: Abstract Self-supervised pretraining has made few-shot learning possible for many NLP tasks. But the pretraining objectives are not typically adapted specifically for in-context few-shot learning. In this paper, we propose to use self-supervision in an intermediate training stage between pretraining and downstream few-shot usage with the goal to teach the model to perform in-context few shot learning.

arxiv-2211-00123.title: SPYGLASS. III. The Fornax-Horologium Association and its Traceback History within the Austral Complex Facilities: Gaia, Las Cumbres Observatory: NRES Spectrograph on 1m Telescope at Sutherland (CPT), Wise (TLV), and Cerro Tololo (LSC) astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , saphires ( Toffle
arxiv-2211-00123.creator: Ronan Kerr, Adam L. Kraus, Simon J. Murphy, Daniel M. Krolikowski, Timothy R. Bedding, Aaron C. Rizzuto
arxiv-2211-00123.description: Abstract The study of young associations is essential for building a complete record of local star formation processes. The Fornax-Horologium association (FH), including the χ 1 \chi^{1} Fornacis cluster, represents one of the nearest young stellar populations to the Sun.

arxiv-2302-10246.title: On the Tremaine-Gunn Limit with Mass-Varying Particles
arxiv-2302-10246.creator: Lotfi Boubekeur, Stefano Profumo
arxiv-2302-10246.description: Abstract General classical arguments on the time evolution of the phase-space density can be used to derive constraints on the mass of particle candidates for the cosmological dark matter (DM). The resulting Tremaine-Gunn limit is extremely useful in constraining particle DM models. In certain models, however, the DM particle mass varies appreciably over time.

arxiv-2305-11220.title: Protecting Quantum Modes in Optical Fibers
arxiv-2305-11220.creator: M. A. T. Butt, P. Roth, G. K. L. Wong, M. H. Frosz, L. L. Sánchez-Soto, E. A. Anashkina, A. V. Andrianov, P. Banzer, P. St.J. Russell, G. Leuchs
arxiv-2305-11220.description: Abstract Polarization-preserving fibers maintain the two polarization states of an orthogonal basis. Quantum communication, however, requires sending at least two nonorthogonal states and these cannot both be preserved. We present a new scheme that allows for using polarization encoding in a fiber not only in the discrete, but also in the continuous-variable regime.

arxiv-2306-01121.title: Differentially Private Episodic Reinforcement Learning with Heavy-tailed Rewards
arxiv-2306-01121.creator: Yulian Wu, Xingyu Zhou, Sayak Ray Chowdhury, Di Wang
arxiv-2306-01121.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yulian Wu, Xingyu Zhou, Sayak Ray Chowdhury, Di Wang. In this paper, we study the problem of (finite horizon tabular) Markov decision processes (MDPs) with heavy-tailed rewards under the constraint of differential privacy (DP).

arxiv-2306-09550.title: Minimizing an Uncrossed Collection of Drawings
arxiv-2306-09550.creator: Petr Hliněný, Tomáš Masařík
arxiv-2306-09550.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce the following new concept in graph drawing. Our task is to find a small collection of drawings such that they all together satisfy some property that is useful for graph visualization. We propose investigating a property where each edge is not crossed in at least one drawing in the collection.

arxiv-2311-10152.title: Quantum tomography of magnons using Brillouin light scattering
arxiv-2311-10152.creator: Sanchar Sharma, Silvia Viola Kusminskiy, Victor A.S.V. Bittencourt
arxiv-2311-10152.description: Abstract Quantum magnonics, an emerging field focusing on the study of magnons for quantum applications, requires precise measurement methods capable of resolving single magnons. Existing techniques introduce additional dissipation channels and are not apt for magnets in free space. Brillouin light scattering (BLS) is a well-established technique for probing the magnetization known for its high sensitivity and temporal resolution.

arxiv-2402-14487.title: Mathematical Modeling and Hyers-Ulam Stability for a Nonlinear Epidemiological Model with Φ p \Phi_{p} Operator and Mittag-Leffler Kernel
arxiv-2402-14487.creator: Achraf Zinihi, Moulay Rchid Sidi Ammi, Matthias Ehrhardt
arxiv-2402-14487.description: Abstract This paper investigates a novel nonlinear singular fractional SI model with the Φ p \Phi_{p} operator and the Mittag-Leffler kernel. The initial investigation includes the existence, uniqueness, boundedness, and non-negativity of the solution. We then establish Hyers-Ulam stability for the proposed model in Banach space.

arxiv-2411-01045.title: Fighting Spurious Correlations in Text Classification via a Causal Learning Perspective
arxiv-2411-01045.creator: Yuqing Zhou, Ziwei Zhu
arxiv-2411-01045.description: Abstract In text classification tasks, models often rely on spurious correlations for predictions, incorrectly associating irrelevant features with the target labels. This issue limits the robustness and generalization of models, especially when faced with out-of-distribution data where such spurious correlations no longer hold.

arxiv-2503-14568.title: Teaching Artificial Intelligence to Perform Rapid, Resolution-Invariant Grain Growth Modeling via Fourier Neural Operator
arxiv-2503-14568.creator: Iman Peivaste, Ahmed Makradi, Salim Belouettar
arxiv-2503-14568.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Iman Peivaste, Ahmed Makradi, Salim Belouettar. Microstructural evolution, particularly grain growth, plays a critical role in shaping the physical, optical, and electronic properties of materials. Traditional phase-field modeling accurately simulates these phenomena but is computationally intensive, especially for large systems and fine spatial resolutions. While machine learning approaches have been employed to accelerate simulations, they often struggle with resolution dependence and generalization across different grain scales.

arxiv-2510-26330.title: Conditioning random points by the number of vertices of their convex hull: the bi-pointed case
arxiv-2510-26330.description: Abstract Pick N N random points U 1 , ⋯ , U N U_{1},\cdots,U_{N} independently and uniformly in a triangle ABC with area 1, and take the convex hull of the set { A , B , U 1 , ⋯ , U N } \{A,B,U_{1},\cdots,U_{N}\} .

arxiv-2601-22249.title: FunPRM: Function-as-Step Process Reward Model with Meta Reward Correction for Code Generation
arxiv-2601-22249.creator: Ruiyi Zhang, Peijia Qin, Qi Cao, Eric Xue, Pengtao Xie
arxiv-2601-22249.description: Abstract Code generation is a core application of large language models (LLMs), yet LLMs still frequently fail on complex programming tasks. Given its success in mathematical reasoning, test-time scaling approaches such as Process Reward Model (PRM)-based Best-of-N selection offer a promising way to improve performance.

arxiv-2603-01547.title: PathMoE: Interpretable Multimodal Interaction Experts for Pediatric Brain Tumor Classification
arxiv-2603-01547.creator: Jian Yu, Joakim Nguyen, Jinrui Fang, Awais Naeem, Zeyuan Cao, Sanjay Krishnan, Nicholas Konz, Tianlong Chen, Chandra Krishnan, Hairong Wang, Edward Castillo, Ying Ding, Ankita Shukla

pmc-12427423.title: Animal Video Lovers Always Have Company: The Role of Cyber-Mediated Animal Attachment in Loneliness
pmc-12427423.creator: Junzi Zhang, Su Tao, Wenchong Du, Cédric Sueur
pmc-12427423.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryMany people enjoy watching cute or heartwarming animal videos online, but little is known about how this activity may affect our emotions. This study explored whether watching animal videos on the internet can help reduce feelings of loneliness. The researchers introduced a new concept called “cyber-mediated animal attachment,” which refers to the emotional connection people can form with animals they see in digital media.

pmc-12514606.title: Machine learning models for predicting transstenotic pressure gradient based on computed tomography angiography features
pmc-12514606.creator: Yan Huang, Xu Han, Xiaoyu Qiu, Chihang Dai, Linkun Cai, Zhiyuan An, Hui Zhang, Guo-Peng Wang, Shusheng Gong, Long Jin, Xue Zhang, Binbin Sui, Zhenghan Yang, Pengfei Zhao, Zhenchang Wang, Heyu Ding
pmc-12514606.description: BackgroundThe transstenotic pressure gradient (TPG) is closely associated with the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment strategies of conditions such as idiopathic intracranial hypertension and pulsatile tinnitus. Currently, TPG assessment relies on invasive, complex, and costly digital subtraction angiography (DSA), and an efficient, noninvasive evaluation method remains lacking.

pmc-12564865.title: Quantum Interference Supernodes, Thermoelectric Enhancement, and the Role of Dephasing
pmc-12564865.creator: Justin P Bergfield, Paolo Bordone, Jan Mol
pmc-12564865.description: Quantum interference can strongly enhance thermoelectric response, with higher-order “supernodes” predicted to yield scalable gains in thermopower and efficiency. A central question, however, is whether such features are intrinsically more fragile to dephasing. Using Büttiker voltage–temperature probes, we establish an order-selection rule: the effective near-node order is set by the lowest among coherent and probe-assisted channels.

pmc-12605537.title: Herbal medicine and acupuncture for mild cognitive impairment: a retrospective study of 2,242 for older adults in Republic of Korea
pmc-12605537.creator: Hyo-Weon Suh, Jae Hwan Lim, Jin-woo Suh, Chan Park, Yong-Sin Park, Sun-Yong Chung
pmc-12605537.description: IntroductionDementia prevalence increases with age, underscoring the importance of early intervention for mild cognitive impairment (MCI). However, standard treatment recommendations for MCI remain lacking. Herbal medicine and acupuncture have been proposed as potential alternatives. This study evaluated the feasibility and effectiveness of these interventions in patients with MCI.

pmc-12732741.title: Methamphetamine-Associated Cardiomyopathy and Cardioembolic Stroke: Brain–Heart–Gut Axis Crosstalk, Diagnostic Strategies, and Anticoagulation Challenges
pmc-12732741.creator: Pei-Jung Lin, Chia-Hui Wu, Jen-Hung Huang, Jakir Hossain Bhuiyan Masud, Chien-Tai Hong, Lung Chan, Chen-Chih Chung
pmc-12732741.description: Methamphetamine (MA) abuse has emerged as a multisystem insult driving cardiovascular and neurovascular consequences. Methamphetamine-associated cardiomyopathy (MACM) remains an underrecognized cause of cardioembolic stroke through left ventricular thrombus (LVT) formation. MA-induced gut dysbiosis and enteric neural disruption exacerbate systemic inflammation and autonomic imbalance, resulting in broader dysregulation of the brain–heart–gut axis.

pmc-12776244.title: Construction of a prognostic model based on efferocytosis for predicting survival and immunotherapy efficacy in cervical cancer
pmc-12776244.creator: Li-Li Zhang, Yan-Fei Ji, Jing Li, Wen-Hao Wang, Yong-Li Hou
pmc-12776244.description: BackgroundCervical cancer (CC) is the foremost contributor to cancer-related mortality among women. Identifying and investigating genes associated with CC prognosis are crucial for improving patient outcomes. Recent advances in high-throughput data analysis methods have revealed a correlation between CC prognosis and the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME).

pmc-13222513.title: Buschke–Lowenstein tumour managed by wide excision and V-Y flap reconstruction: report of two cases
pmc-13222513.creator: Miroslav Zashev, Nevrie Niyazi
pmc-13222513.description: Buschke–Lowenstein tumour (giant condyloma acuminatum) is a rare sexually transmitted lesion associated with human papillomavirus infection, most commonly types 6 and 11. Although histologically benign, it demonstrates locally aggressive growth, high recurrence rates, and potential malignant transformation. We report two cases of large circumferential Buschke–Lowenstein tumours involving the anorectal region.

pmc-13230644.title: Multimodal deep feature fusion with transformer for brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging
pmc-13230644.creator: M Pajany, K Boopalan, R Rajesh, W JaiSingh, Bibhuti Bhusan Dash, Saroja Kumar Rout, P Pavan Kumar
pmc-13230644.description: Brain tumors (BTs) arise due to abnormal cell growth, which has a high mortality rate globally. Millions of lives can be saved through the timely identification of BT. Precise identification and segmentation of BTs are essential to enhance the precision of analysis and the efficiency of therapeutic strategies. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a broadly utilized analytical tool.

pmc-13314014.title: Utility of large mitochondrial rRNA sequences in phylogenetic inference of some epinephelinae species from the Egyptian Red Sea
pmc-13314014.creator: Mohammad Allam, Ali H. Abu Almaaty, Layla Omran Elmajdoub, Maryham M. Aziz
pmc-13314014.description: Background:Grouper fishes have a diverse variety of shapes and colors, making it difficult to accurately perform morphological identification. In addition, certain unique grouper species may be included in the same species description due to morphological similarities.Aim:The main purpose of this study was to investigate the evolutionary relationships between various species of the family Epinephelinae using the large mitochondrial rRNA gene.

pmc-13566686.title: Overview of Non-Cirrhotic Portal Hypertension in Pediatric Patients
pmc-13566686.creator: Ambika Walecha, Senthilkumar Sankararaman, Kadakkal Radhakrishnan
pmc-13566686.description: Non-cirrhotic portal hypertension (NCPHT) is defined as portal hypertension (PHT) occurring in the absence of cirrhosis. Major etiological causes of NCPHT include immunological disorders, chronic infections, exposure to medications or toxins, prothrombotic conditions, and several genetic syndromes, highlighting that NCPHT is not a single disease but a shared phenotype arising from diverse underlying pathways.

pmc-13592087.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in antifungal immunity: mechanisms, dual roles, regulatory networks, and clinical perspectives
pmc-13592087.creator: Han Li, Guanzhi Chen, Lingyue Sun
pmc-13592087.description: Invasive fungal diseases (IFDs) are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are a key effector mechanism of innate antifungal immunity, but they may also act as a double-edged sword. This review summarizes the biological basis of NETs, with an emphasis on lytic and non-lytic NET formation.

pmc-13623774.title: The natural history of untreated small (< 5 mm) intracranial aneurysms: a five-year angiographic follow-up study
pmc-13623774.creator: Jefferson Rosi, Juliana Gozzo Sekula, Leonardo B. O. Brenner, Manoel Jacobsen Teixeira, Saul Almeida da Silva, Jose Guilherme Mendes Pereira Caldas, Carlos Gilberto Carlotti Junior, Eberval Gadelha Figueiredo
